purpose: Study-to-node evidence for the parallel fieldstate-asfr-v2 route. No entry is a TFR coefficient.

records.citation: Blackman CF et al. A role for the magnetic field in the radiation-induced efflux of calcium ions from brain tissue in vitro. Bioelectromagnetics. 1985;6:327-337.
records.system: Chick brain tissue
records.field_class: ELF electric field with altered local geomagnetic background
records.finding: Changing the local geomagnetic field shifted which ELF frequencies changed calcium efflux.
records.translation_scope: Supports background-dependent field-state measurement; it does not estimate a human reproductive or TFR effect.

records.citation: Ritz T et al. Resonance effects indicate a radical-pair mechanism for avian magnetic compass. Nature. 2004;429:177-180.
records.system: European robins
records.field_class: Oscillating RF magnetic field with controlled angle to geomagnetic field
records.finding: Orientation disruption depended on the relative angle between the RF and static background fields.
records.translation_scope: Supports a vector/angle signature for radical-pair magnetoreception; it is not a human reproductive study.
limitations: Does not identify a human receptor

records.citation: Usselman RJ et al. The quantum biology of reactive oxygen species partitioning impacts cellular bioenergetics. Scientific Reports. 2016;6:38543.
records.system: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells and radical-pair chemistry system
records.field_class: 1.4 MHz RF magnetic field with 50 microtesla static field and controlled orientation
records.finding: Field orientation changed radical-pair ROS product yield and endothelial bioenergetic readouts.
records.translation_scope: Supports a geometry-sensitive ROS intermediate; it does not quantify organ-specific fertility capacity.
limitations: Exposure setup is not a population dose

records.citation: Majewska M et al. European Robin Cryptochrome-4a Associates with Lipid Bilayers in an Ordered Manner, Fulfilling a Molecular-Level Condition for Magnetoreception. ACS Chemical Biology. 2025.
records.study_type: Biophysical protein-membrane experiment and molecular simulation
records.system: European robin Cry4a and model lipid bilayers
records.field_class: Receptor geometry / membrane anchoring study
records.finding: Cry4a associated with lipid bilayers in an ordered manner controlled by membrane physical state.
records.translation_scope: Supports the need to model receptor orientation and membrane state; it does not establish a human cryptochrome fertility pathway.
limitations: No applied exposure or reproductive endpoint

records.citation: Zandieh A et al. An amplification mechanism for weak ELF magnetic fields quantum-bio effects in cancer cells. Scientific Reports. 2025;15:2964.
records.system: Cancer cell lines
records.field_class: ELF magnetic fields from 0.01 to 5 Hz and 0 to 100 mT
records.finding: Mitochondrial membrane-potential and ROS responses varied with field frequency, including 0.02 and 0.04 Hz conditions.
records.translation_scope: Supports testing a cell-state-dependent envelope/resonance feature; it is not evidence for RF network modulation or a reproductive TFR coefficient.

records.citation: Sherrard RM et al. Low-intensity electromagnetic fields induce human cryptochrome to modulate intracellular reactive oxygen species. PLOS Biology. 2018;16:e2006229.
records.study_type: Controlled cell experiment with cryptochrome loss-of-function
records.system: Human HEK293 cells and mouse embryonic fibroblasts
records.field_class: Weak pulsed electromagnetic fields
records.finding: Field-associated ROS and response-gene changes required cryptochrome in the tested cell systems.
records.translation_scope: Directly informs the CRY-to-ROS bridge in cells; it does not specify RF device exposure, gonadal dose, or fertility effect size.

records.citation: Cao H et al. Effects of 1.8 GHz radiofrequency fields on circadian rhythms of melatonin, GSH-Px and SOD in rats. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 2015;12:2071-2087.
records.system: Rats
records.field_class: 1.8 GHz RF exposure at six time-of-day conditions
records.finding: Melatonin and antioxidant rhythm measures varied by the RF exposure time in the experimental protocol.
records.translation_scope: Supports an explicit circadian/redox context in FieldState; it does not estimate human conception or birth rates.
limitations: Hormone and antioxidant endpoints rather than fertility

records.citation: De Iuliis GN et al. Mobile phone radiation induces reactive oxygen species production and DNA damage in human spermatozoa in vitro. PLOS ONE. 2009;4:e6446.
records.system: Purified human spermatozoa
records.field_class: 1.8 GHz RF-EMR, 0.4 to 27.5 W/kg SAR
records.finding: In the exposure system, increasing SAR was accompanied by mitochondrial ROS, oxidative DNA damage and DNA fragmentation, with lower motility and vitality.
records.translation_scope: Direct human gamete endpoint evidence; in-vitro exposure and dose range do not provide a population TFR coefficient.
limitations: Dose/exposure context differs from population monitoring

records.citation: Yu G et al. Long-term exposure to 4G smartphone radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation diminished male reproductive potential by directly disrupting Spock3-MMP2-BTB axis in the testes of adult rats. Science of the Total Environment. 2020;698:133860.
records.study_type: Controlled adult-rat local exposure experiment with mechanistic rescue
records.system: Adult rat testes
records.field_class: Localized 4G smartphone RF exposure to the scrotal region
records.finding: The study reported delayed sperm/reproductive changes and a Spock3-MMP2 blood-testis-barrier axis; Spock3 inhibition was used as a mechanistic rescue.
records.translation_scope: Strong structure evidence for a local BTB branch; it is a rat study and does not calibrate human local transfer or TFR.

records.citation: Meena R et al. Therapeutic approaches of melatonin in microwave radiations-induced oxidative stress-mediated toxicity on male fertility pattern of Wistar rats. Electromagnetic Biology and Medicine. 2014;33:81-91.
records.study_type: Controlled animal experiment with melatonin intervention
records.system: Wistar rat testes and semen endpoints
records.field_class: 2.45 GHz microwave exposure, reported SAR 0.14 W/kg
records.finding: The study reported redox, testosterone, sperm and DNA-fragmentation changes with attenuation in its melatonin intervention arm.
records.translation_scope: Supports a redox-mediated testis branch and a mediator test; it is not a human prevention recommendation or effect-size calibration.

records.citation: Ahmadi SS et al. Effect of non-ionizing electromagnetic field on the alteration of ovarian follicles in rats. Electron Physician. 2016;8:2168-2174.
records.system: Rat ovaries exposed during intrauterine and postnatal development
records.field_class: 50 Hz magnetic field exposure for 8 or 13 weeks
records.finding: The study reported increased follicular atresia and ovarian/oocyte morphological changes after the protocol.
records.translation_scope: Supports an explicit developmental ovarian-reserve state; it is a rat histology study, not an estimate of human ovarian reserve decline.
limitations: No human AMH/AFC or fertility calibration

records.citation: Lochhead JJ et al. Oxidative stress increases blood-brain barrier permeability and induces alterations in occludin. Journal of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism. 2010.
records.system: Rat blood-brain barrier
records.field_class: Oxidative stress manipulation, not EMF exposure
records.finding: Oxidative stress increased BBB permeability and altered occludin localization; antioxidant treatment attenuated the reported change.
records.translation_scope: Supports the redox-to-tight-junction link needed by the BBB branch; it is not direct EMF evidence.

records.citation: Chakraborty P et al. Excess iodine impairs spermatogenesis by inducing oxidative stress and perturbing blood-testis barrier. Reproductive Toxicology. 2020;96:128-140.
records.system: Rat testis and blood-testis barrier
records.field_class: Oxidative-stress manipulation, not EMF exposure
records.finding: Oxidative stress was accompanied by reduced BTB junction proteins and adverse sperm endpoints in the study model.
records.translation_scope: Supports the redox-to-BTB-to-sperm segment as a biological bridge; it is not direct EMF evidence.
limitations: Endpoint mapping to human fecundability is not estimated

records.citation: Liu Y et al. The circadian clock protein Bmal1 regulates progesterone synthesis in mice. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2014;111:13231-13236.
records.system: Mouse ovarian steroidogenic cells
records.field_class: Downstream circadian mechanism, not EMF exposure
records.finding: Ovarian Bmal1 disruption impaired steroidogenic progesterone support and implantation in the experimental system.
records.translation_scope: Supports the clock-to-steroidogenesis-to-implantation segment; it does not establish an EMF-to-Bmal1 effect size.

records.citation: He C et al. Melatonin synthesis in the mitochondria of murine oocytes and its role in protecting oocytes from oxidative damage. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2016;17:939.
records.system: Murine oocytes and embryo-development endpoints
records.field_class: Downstream redox/melatonin mechanism, not EMF exposure
records.finding: Melatonin/redox manipulation changed mitochondrial and oxidative-damage markers and embryo-development measures in the study system.
records.translation_scope: Supports the oocyte redox-resilience state; it is not direct EMF evidence or a human IVF prediction.

records.citation: Cordelli E et al. Effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure on male fertility: A systematic review of experimental studies on non-human mammals and human sperm in vitro. Environment International. 2024;185:108509.
records.system: Non-human mammals and human sperm in vitro
records.field_class: RF-EMF from 100 kHz to 300 GHz
records.finding: The review reported lower pregnancy rate (moderate certainty) and lower sperm count (low certainty), no litter-size effect (moderate certainty), and very-low certainty for several other pooled endpoints.
records.translation_scope: Provides review-level context for male reproductive branches; it is not an individual human exposure study and does not supply a TFR coefficient.
limitations: Mostly non-human mammals and human sperm in vitro
Exposure relevance and thermal conditions vary
Pregnancy-rate analysis was later corrected and is sensitive to a high-SAR study

records.citation: Cordelli E et al. Corrigendum to Effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure on male fertility. Environment International. 2025;199:109449.
records.system: Re-analysis of the 2024 review data
records.field_class: RF-EMF evidence synthesis
records.finding: The correction revised the pregnancy-rate meta-analysis; the revised result is partly driven by a high-SAR study and becomes non-significant when that study is excluded.
records.translation_scope: Constrains interpretation of the review evidence and must accompany the 2024 record; it is not a population TFR result.

records.citation: Naderi N et al. Influence of radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation on spermatogenesis and sperm function in rodent models: A systematic review. Reproductive Toxicology. 2026;144:109300.
records.system: Rat and mouse spermatogenesis/sperm studies
records.field_class: 800 to 24,000 MHz RF-EMR; reported SAR range 0.014 to 34 W/kg
records.finding: The review identified 88 eligible rodent studies and organised sperm, oxidative-stress, DNA-damage, apoptosis, histopathology and hormone endpoints.
records.translation_scope: Supports the multi-endpoint male branch and a structured parameter-search agenda; heterogeneity prevents a single cross-study biological coefficient.
limitations: Heterogeneous exposure, dosimetry and risk-of-bias reporting
Does not identify a uniform causal interpretation or human TFR coefficient

records.citation: Baldini GM et al. Does Electromagnetic Pollution in the ART Laboratory Affect Sperm Quality? A Cross-Sectional Observational Study. Toxics. 2025;13:510.
records.system: Semen samples from 102 healthy males in an IVF laboratory
records.field_class: One-hour close-distance exposure to smartphone or 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi repeater versus laboratory comparators
records.finding: The report found lower progressive motility in the mobile-phone and Wi-Fi-repeater exposure conditions than in its comparator conditions.
records.translation_scope: A close-distance, short-term human-sperm endpoint study that informs local-geometry measurement; it is not a personal exposure cohort or TFR estimate.
limitations: Cross-sectional/comparator design does not establish population exposure-response

records.citation: Calis P et al. Does Exposure of Smart Phones during Pregnancy Affect the Offspring's Ovarian Reserve? A Rat Model Study. Fetal and Pediatric Pathology. 2021;40:142-152.
records.system: Female rat offspring ovarian histology at postnatal day 42
records.field_class: Smartphone RF exposure during pregnancy
records.finding: The exposed offspring group had fewer primordial and secondary follicles and higher atresia in the reported protocol.
records.translation_scope: Supports a developmental ovarian-reserve branch distinct from acute ovulation; it is not a human reserve calibration.
limitations: Pregnancy exposure protocol is not a measured human FieldState
Histology endpoint rather than adult fertility

records.citation: Yousefi B et al. Impairment of Oogenesis and Folliculogenesis in Neonatal Rats after Maternal Exposure to Mobile Phones. Reproductive Sciences. 2025;32:2259-2269.
records.system: Neonatal Wistar-rat ovaries after maternal phone exposure
records.field_class: Maternal mobile-phone exposure during gestation
records.finding: The primary animal study evaluates oogenesis, folliculogenesis and neonatal ovarian hormonal/developmental endpoints after its maternal exposure protocol.
records.translation_scope: Adds a recent developmental female branch; it is a primary rat study, not a human review or a direct TFR coefficient.
limitations: Neonatal endpoints require longitudinal human translation

records.citation: Iolchiev BS et al. Geomagnetic activity and sperm quality in Holstein bulls. Agricultural Biology. 2019;54:1196-1205.
records.system: Ten Holstein bulls and repeated semen samples
records.field_class: Natural geomagnetic activity index
records.finding: The report associated higher geomagnetic-activity periods with changes in ejaculate volume, motility, morphology and DNA fragmentation measures.
records.translation_scope: A natural-field sentinel for background-state hypotheses; observational association does not isolate geomagnetism from time-varying covariates or generalise to humans.
limitations: Livestock management and seasonality may confound

records.citation: BERM reproducibility analysis using UN World Population Prospects 2024 ASFR and World Bank/ITU mobile subscriptions, 2000-2023.
records.system: Country-level WPP ASFR and World Bank/ITU mobile-subscription series
records.field_class: Technology-adoption timing proxy, not physical FieldState
records.finding: The analysis reports an age-cohort contrast consistent with the developmental-memory premise; the input mobile series is explicitly retained as a timing proxy.
records.translation_scope: Tests the predicted age/cohort signature, not a causal EMF effect or a FieldState transfer coefficient.
limitations: Versioned scenario weights are not calibrated sensitivity estimates
Mobile subscriptions are not an EMF dose
Development, policy, tempo and demand covary with adoption

records.citation: Shafik A, Ibrahim IH, El-Sayed EM. Effect of different types of textile fabric on spermatogenesis. I. Electrostatic potentials generated on surface of human scrotum by wearing different types of fabric. Andrologia. 1992;24:145-147.
records.system: Twenty-one healthy adult men wearing polyester, polyester/cotton or cotton underpants
records.field_class: Triboelectric textile–skin interface; historical physically underdetermined V/cm² reading
records.finding: The reported instrument readings ranked 100% polyester above a 50:50 polyester/cotton blend, while cotton had no detected reading in the stated setup.
records.translation_scope: Supports a material-dependent human textile–skin static-interface state; the historically reported, physically underdetermined V/cm² reading is not sufficient to calculate Q, V/m or an organ field without probe geometry, reference and calibration.
limitations: Reported V/cm² is not a standard potential, field or charge-density unit
Probe geometry and earth/body reference are incompletely reported
No reproductive endpoint in this measurement study

records.citation: Shafik A. Contraceptive efficacy of polyester-induced azoospermia in normal men. Contraception. 1992;45:439-451.
records.system: Fourteen adult men wearing a polyester scrotal sling continuously for 12 months
records.field_class: Triboelectric textile–skin interface with altered scrotal geometry
records.finding: The report described reversible azoospermia, seminiferous-tubule changes and static-interface readings during the sling period; it explicitly proposed both electrostatic and thermoregulatory mechanisms.
records.translation_scope: A human reproductive endpoint anchor for a prolonged textile-interface configuration; it does not isolate the static component, provide intragonadal E-field dosimetry or calibrate a general clothing or TFR effect.
limitations: Static component and altered scrotal thermoregulation co-occurred
No measured Q, calibrated V/m, dE/dt or organ-transfer model

records.citation: Dincmen MG, Hauser PJ, Gursoy NC. Atmospheric Pressure Plasma Treatment of Nylon 6,6 and Polyester Fabrics for Enhancing Antistatic Properties. AATCC Journal of Research. 2016;3:36-46.
records.study_type: Controlled textile-material charge generation and dissipation experiment
records.system: Untreated and plasma/antistatic-treated polyester and nylon fabrics
records.field_class: Triboelectric charge generation, surface resistivity and charge-decay measurements
records.finding: Under the reported textile test conditions, untreated polyester had a large retained charge and half-life over 2,000 seconds, while antistatic treatment reduced both charge magnitude and decay time.
records.translation_scope: Supports explicit material-treatment and relaxation-time variables in a static-interface FieldState; it is not a human skin, organ or reproductive experiment.
limitations: Fabric-material test rather than textile–skin contact
Specific plasma/chemical treatment and climate conditions

records.citation: England SJ, Lihou K, Robert D. Static electricity passively attracts ticks onto hosts. Current Biology. 2023;33:3041-3047.e4.
records.study_type: Controlled arthropod electrostatic-attraction experiment with finite-element modelling
records.system: Ixodes ricinus nymphs and host–vegetation electrostatic geometries
records.field_class: Static host–vegetation air-gap electric fields and field gradients
records.finding: Ixodes ricinus nymphs crossed short air gaps toward charged host-like targets; polarity independence supported induced polarization, and host–vegetation modelling showed local fields exceeding 300 kV/m in the stated geometry.
records.translation_scope: Directly supports an electrostatic contact/attachment branch for the tested tick and geometry; it does not establish RF/ELF resistance, a population abundance effect or a human reproductive coefficient.
limitations: Attachment/attraction endpoint rather than population growth
Field-gradient and morphology must be measured for each host/habitat configuration

records.citation: Colin ME, Richard D, Fourcassie V, Belzunces LP. Attraction of Varroa jacobsoni, parasite of Apis mellifera by electrical charges. Journal of Insect Physiology. 1992;38:111-117.
records.system: Varroa jacobsoni as named in the original study (now generally treated as V. destructor in this Apis mellifera pest context) and honey-bee-range charged lures
records.field_class: Static electrical charges matched to the reported host range
records.finding: Charge sign altered mite movement and a negatively charged lure increased contact and climbing in the experimental system.
records.translation_scope: Supports a charge-sensitive parasite contact/behavior branch; it does not estimate Varroa population growth, colony collapse or resistance to other field classes.
limitations: Original historical taxonomic name is retained with its modern interpretation stated
Laboratory lure rather than a whole colony
Contact behavior does not establish fitness or resistance

records.citation: Mallinson VJ, Woodburn FA, O'Reilly LJ. Weak anthropogenic electric fields affect honeybee foraging. iScience. 2025;28:112550.
records.study_type: Paired field experiment with anthropogenic AC/DC electric-field treatments
records.system: Honeybee floral landing behavior in urban meadows
records.field_class: Weak 50 Hz AC and DC aerial electric fields; transmission-line field measurements
records.finding: In the reported paired experiment, AC and positive DC treatments reduced honeybee floral landings, while negative DC did not show a statistically significant effect; line measurements documented comparable field ranges at foraging height.
records.translation_scope: Directly supports a component- and polarity-specific pollinator behavior branch; it does not quantify colony fitness, ecosystem abundance or a general EMF effect.
limitations: AC/DC E-field conditions should not be merged with RF or magnetic-field hypotheses

records.citation: García-Robledo C, Dierick D, Manser K. Electric transportation and electroreception in hummingbird flower mites. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2025;122:e2419214122.
records.study_type: Controlled mite behavior, sensory-ablation and electrostatic-transport experiment
records.system: Tropical hummingbird flower mites and hummingbird-like electric-field configurations
records.field_class: Modulated and static electric fields with host-like charge and geometry
records.finding: The tested flower mites responded to modulated fields using front-leg sensory structures and used electrostatic attraction to bridge a gap to a hummingbird-beak analogue.
records.translation_scope: Directly supports an electroreception-plus-transport mechanism in a mite ecological life cycle; it does not show that all ticks or mites share the same response spectrum.
limitations: Tropical flower-mite guild rather than Ixodes
No multigeneration selection or population estimate

records.citation: Šofranková L, Baňas M, Pipová N, et al. Effects of Electromagnetic Radiation on Neuropeptide Transcript Levels in the Synganglion of Ixodes ricinus. Pathogens. 2023;12:1398.
records.study_type: Controlled radiofrequency exposure and tick synganglion qRT-PCR experiment
records.system: Adult male and female Ixodes ricinus exposed to a 900 MHz RF field at stated 2 or 40 V/m conditions and durations
records.field_class: 900 MHz polarized, unmodulated RF electric-field exposure
records.finding: The reported 900 MHz exposures produced sex-, intensity- and time-dependent changes in neuropeptide and receptor transcript levels in Ixodes ricinus synganglia; the stronger condition had suppressory effects after stated exposures.
records.translation_scope: Supports a separate tick RF physiology branch and the need for component-specific transfer functions; it does not measure static attachment, RF resistance, feeding fitness, population growth or human outcomes.
limitations: Transcript endpoint rather than organismal fitness
Exposure geometry and thermal control determine interpretation

records.citation: Morley EL, Robert D. Electric Fields Elicit Ballooning in Spiders. Current Biology. 2018;28:2324-2330.e2.
records.study_type: Controlled arthropod behavior and mechanosensory-hair experiment
records.system: Ballooning spiders
records.field_class: Vertical atmospheric-scale static electric fields
records.finding: Electric fields commensurate with atmospheric conditions elicited ballooning behavior and mechanically activated spider sensory hairs in the reported experiments.
records.translation_scope: Supports an electric-field-to-dispersal behavioral branch; it does not estimate landscape population expansion or the effects of built electrical infrastructure.
limitations: Atmospheric electric field rather than textile interface
Dispersal behavior is not a population-growth estimate

records.citation: BERM internal analysis. Nike-BBS spatial gradient reinterpreted through peak field physics. 2026. Underlying data: USGS North American Breeding Bird Survey.
records.study_type: Internal spatial analysis with peak-field reinterpretation
records.system: 1,381 BBS bird survey routes near 268 Nike radar sites (141 active 1966), trends 1966-1980
records.field_class: Pulsed S-band radar sidelobe peak field (1 MW, 1 µs pulse, 400 Hz PRF, 2° beam)
records.finding: The monotonic distance gradient (Spearman ρ = +0.088, p = 0.001) is consistent with 1/r² peak field attenuation when 85% of BERM pathways (VGIC 45%, CRY/RPM 25%, HPA 15%) respond to peak field rather than RMS. Peak sidelobe field at 1 km: 24.5 V/m vs RMS 0.037 V/m (ratio 671:1). BERM sigmoid S(E_peak) reaches 50% at 95 km (S(E_rms) at 0.14 km). CRY radical-pair lifetime (~1 µs) matches radar pulse duration.
records.translation_scope: Supports the distinction between peak-field and RMS-field biological relevance for pulsed sources. It does not prove causation: the gradient is correlational (Spearman p = 0.001; the <50 km vs >100 km trend contrast is Welch p = 0.031) and competing explanations (habitat, urbanization) are not excluded.
limitations: No measured field dosimetry at routes
Habitat and urbanization confounders not fully controlled
VGIC threshold exceedance at 24.5 V/m is a prediction, not confirmed by cell experiment
Site closure did not predict bird recovery, which constrains the causal reading
